questions.q: What is a module in Python?
options: A .py file whose functions other files can use with import
questions.explain: money.py is the module money. import money (or from money import rupees) lets other files use its code without copying it.

questions.q: After import money, how do you call its rupees function?
questions.explain: With import money, names are used through the module: money.rupees. With from money import rupees, you can call rupees() directly.

questions.q: Where do json, datetime and random come from?
options: Python's standard library: they come with Python, ready to import
They are downloaded from GitHub on every run
questions.explain: The standard library ships with Python. Third-party packages like Django are installed separately (Module 5).

questions.q: money.py ends with if __name__ == "__main__": print(...). When does that print run?
options: Only when you run python3 money.py directly
questions.explain: The file you run is named "__main__". An imported module gets its own name ("money"), so the block is skipped on import.

questions.q: For python3 main.py search box, what is sys.argv[1:]?
questions.explain: sys.argv is every word after python3, starting with the script's name. [1:] skips the script name.

questions.q: In Bazaar v0, why does catalog.py raise errors instead of printing them?
options: So the rules work anywhere: main.py (or later a website) decides how to show the problem
questions.explain: Rules live in catalog.py and return or raise; main.py is the only part that talks to the person. The same catalog.py could sit behind a website.

questions.q: (Going deeper) You name your own file json.py. What happens to import json in that folder?
options: Python always picks the standard library
Python imports YOUR json.py, which has no dumps, so you get an AttributeError
questions.explain: The script's own folder comes first in sys.path. Python 3.13 even suggests renaming the file. Never reuse standard module names.

questions.explain: Packages group related modules. Django apps are packages; python3 -m runs a module by its import name.
